compound-interest.title: 5% nominal, daily compounding
compound-interest.inputs: Start with $10,000, add $200 at each month end for ten years, and enter a 5% nominal annual rate compounded daily. Annual additions, interest tax and inflation are zero.
steps: Convert the daily nominal growth factor to a monthly equivalent: (1 + 0.05/365)^(365/12) − 1.
Grow the starting balance over 120 months and add the future value of the 120 end-month deposits. Compare against the 5% nominal monthly-compounding case with the same deposits.

compound-interest.title: Same yield, converted daily rate
compound-interest.inputs: Use the same $10,000 start, $200 end-month deposits and ten-year horizon. Daily compounding uses a converted nominal annual rate of approximately 4.9899532382%, with no annual additions, tax or inflation.
steps: Find the effective annual growth factor of the monthly quote: (1 + 0.05/12)^12.
Convert that factor to a daily nominal quote: 365 × [(1 + 0.05/12)^(12/365) − 1].
The complete preset retains more rate digits than this explanation. Equal effective yield and equal monthly deposit timing give the same modeled ending balance.

compound-interest.title: 5% monthly, 3% inflation
compound-interest.inputs: Start with $10,000 and add $200 at each month end for ten years. Use a 5% nominal annual rate compounded monthly, 3% annual inflation and zero annual additions or interest tax.
steps: Calculate the nominal balance using the monthly rate of 0.05/12.
Divide the nominal ending balance by 1.03^10 to express purchasing power in starting-period dollars. Contributions and nominal earnings are unchanged by the inflation input.

boat-loan.title: 10 years, USD 20,000 down
boat-loan.inputs: Boat price $50,000; cash down payment $20,000; trade value $0; entered sales tax 7% and $500 fees financed; assumed annual interest 7%; term ten years.
steps: Use 120 monthly payments and a periodic rate of 0.07/12 in the fixed-payment formula.
Compare with $10,000 down under the same purchase and rate assumptions. Upfront cash increases by $10,000; down payment is separate from loan interest and ownership expenses.

savings.title: Earlier deadline: 36 months
savings.inputs: Current savings $2,000; nominal target $20,000; deadline three years; constant 4% APY; end-month deposits; no annual deposits, interest-tax haircut or inflation adjustment.
steps: Use the APY monthly equivalent r = 1.04^(1/12) − 1 and 36 monthly periods.
Compare the shorter deadline against the same target funded over 60 months; the deadline changes, not the assumed return.

savings.title: Time needed with USD 400 monthly
savings.inputs: Current savings $2,000; nominal target $20,000; monthly deposit $400 at month end; constant 4% APY; no annual additions, tax or inflation adjustment.
steps: Use the APY monthly equivalent and grow savings between each monthly deposit.
Find the first whole month at which the balance reaches or exceeds $20,000.
Compare against $300 monthly deposits under the same starting balance, target, yield and timing. The monthly budget changes; the final balance may exceed the target.
